is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

recently_moved_to_uk.description: Whether the claimant has recently moved to the UK.

right_to_reside_status.description: A plain English description of the claimant's right-to-reside position.

Great! I'm here to help you check your Child Benefit eligibility. Let me start by asking about your child.

**How old is your child?**

I need to know if they are:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old
- 20 or over

This helps determine the initial eligibility pathway.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're right, let me continue with the assessment based on your situation. You mentioned you're asking about Alex, who is 3 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. You mentioned you live in the UK and have recently moved here, but your right-to-reside position is not known.

**Let me ask some important questions about your residency status:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This means the UK is your main home where you live on a regular basis)

2. **Do you have any of the following?**
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
   - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
   - Are you working in the UK (or expecting to earn above the National Insurance threshold)?
   - Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

Understanding your residency status is crucial for determining eligibility. Can you tell me more about your immigration status or right to reside in the UK?

conversation.text:
Excellent news! Based on the assessment, **you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**.

## ✅ You Meet All the Requirements

Here's why you qualify:
- ✅ Alex is 3 years old (under 16)
- ✅ Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week
- ✅ Alex isn't receiving qualifying benefits in their own right
- ✅ Alex isn't in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You live in the UK (meeting residency requirements)
- ✅ You have responsibility for Alex (you live together)
- ✅ No one else is claiming for Alex who has priority
- ✅ Alex isn't in local authority care
- ✅ The local council isn't paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

## 📝 Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware** of the High Income Child Benefit Charge if you or your partner earns over £60,000
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

**More information:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
